root_cause.text: The `smc_clc_wait_msg()` function unconditionally accessed the link group (`smc->conn.lgr`) state when handling CLC decline messages during early handshake stages, before the connection had been associated with a link group, causing a null pointer dereference or use-after-free.
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds a guard condition `smc->conn.lgr` to the existing link-group state update logic. The original code at lines 791-792 checked only for the `SMC_FIRST_CONTACT_MASK` flag and then immediately accessed `smc->conn.lgr->sync_err` without verifying that `smc->conn.lgr` was non-null. The fix changes this to `(dclc->hdr.typev2 & SMC_FIRST_CONTACT_MASK) && smc->conn.lgr`, ensuring the link group exists before accessing its state. The commit message explicitly states: "A CLC decline can be received while the handshake is still in an early stage, before the connection has been associated with a link group" and "that state only exists after link group setup has completed."
